svg.title: Personal movement memory and anonymous scent ownership
svg.desc: Two optional sources append inputs to each animal's brain. Personal sighting buffers retain only observed targets; the world stores merged species/sex ground traces. Checkpoints preserve both, while replay stores sampled inputs only.
svg.text: Two optional senses, separate owners
No target IDs in brain inputs; no hidden movement backfill; no compulsory pursuit action.
Observer: private visual memory
Current visibility + distance-ranked top-K targets
Match personal sightings by internal identity.
Ring of H+1 sighting frames
Only selected animals; gaps remain unknown.
Last position, velocity estimate and fading confidence.
World: anonymous ground scent
Dry cell + species + sex → latest deposit time
Overlapping group trails merge; old entries expire.
Local dry-path sampling → nine sectors per group
Several directions can be fresh simultaneously.
No individual destination, full route or consent signal.
Per-animal observation → independent policy
Existing blocks → movement block → species/sex scent blocks
Exact checkpoint
Versioned sensory state + existing world/brains
Restore private buffers and sparse integer deposits.
GRPO trials own copies; newborns inherit no memories.
Sampled replay → selected inspector
Existing input vectors in binary/compressed chunks
Observed movement dots + anonymous scent grids.
No per-frame scent maps; no extra trajectory archive.
Both off by default. Learning decisions, mating proximity and physical challenge gates remain separate.
